handoff_payload.answer_text: Gross margin is not a useful metric for American Express because, as a financial-services company, interest expense and credit-loss provisions are integral to its economics rather than conventional cost of goods sold. A more relevant surplus margin after credit provisions and expenses fell from 24.40% in FY2021 to 18.91% in FY2022, a 5.49-percentage-point decline, as expenses increased by USD 7,985 million and provisions for credit losses increased by USD 3,601 million, despite revenue growth of 24.74%.
